skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides developers through root-cause investigation before fixing bugs, test failures, flaky tests, and unexpected software behavior.
skill.summary: A structured debugging workflow for finding root causes before changing code.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, and documentation examples. Real risk remains in the main guidance for printing environment and signing diagnostics, plus the bundled shell script that executes npm tests. No prompt-injection attempt, malicious persistence, or data-exfiltration code was found.

remediation.issue: Sensitive diagnostics can leak environment or signing metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Replace env dumps with redacted presence checks, and warn users before listing signing identities or writing diagnostics to shared logs.

remediation.issue: The find-polluter.sh helper executes npm tests in the current repository.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the script is opt-in, should run only in trusted repositories, and may execute package scripts. Avoid suppressing all output by default.

remediation.issue: The shell helper handles file lists with whitespace-sensitive looping.
remediation.suggestion: Use null-delimited find output and a while-read loop so unusual test paths do not change behavior or hide failures.

remediation.issue: The creation log exposes a local private configuration path.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute hidden-file path with a generic source description before publishing the marketplace package.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Diagnostic Logging Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The main skill suggests debugging commands such as env grep for IDENTITY and keychain identity listing. In CI or shared logs, this can expose secret values or signing metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance appears in the primary skill instructions and targets secrets, environment propagation, and signing state. The commands are examples, but users may copy them into CI logs.

semantic_findings.title: Bundled Test Runner Executes Project Code
semantic_findings.description: The find-polluter helper discovers test files and runs npm test for each match. Running this in an untrusted repository can execute arbitrary package scripts while suppressing output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The executable shell script directly invokes npm test on discovered paths. This is expected debugging behavior, but it creates a real execution risk in untrusted projects.

content.value_statement: Random fixes waste time and create regressions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through root-cause debugging before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides a four-phase debugging process from investigation to verified implementation.
Helps trace bad values backward through call stacks to find the original trigger.
Provides condition-based waiting patterns for flaky asynchronous tests.
Explains defense-in-depth validation after the root cause is known.
Includes a helper script for finding tests that create unwanted files or state.
limitations: It does not diagnose bugs without project evidence, logs, or reproduction steps.
The included shell script should only run inside trusted repositories.
Some examples require adaptation to local test frameworks and build tools.
It prioritizes correctness over fast speculative fixes.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Use the process to reproduce a failure, inspect recent changes, and confirm one root-cause hypothesis before editing code.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Async Tests
use_cases.description: Replace timing guesses with condition-based waiting patterns and clear timeout messages.

use_cases.title: Review Repeated Failed Fixes
use_cases.description: Pause after multiple failed fixes, reassess architecture, and avoid stacking unrelated changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging on this failing test: [test name]. Error: [message]. Start with evidence gathering and do not propose fixes yet.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Bad Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this bad value backward through the call stack: [value and symptom]. Identify where it first becomes wrong before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Stabilize a Flaky Test
prompt_templates.prompt: This test uses sleeps and fails intermittently: [summary]. Find the real condition to wait for and propose a minimal verification plan.

prompt_templates.title: Reassess Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: I tried these fixes and they failed: [list]. Apply the systematic process, question the architecture if needed, and define the next experiment.

output_examples.input: A payment test sometimes returns pending status instead of completed status.
output_examples.output: The skill would ask for reproduction steps, recent changes, event timing evidence, and the first point where status stops updating.

output_examples.input: A git operation runs in the wrong directory during tests.
output_examples.output: The skill would trace the directory value back through callers, identify the source of the empty path, and add validation at several layers.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes changed different parts of a shared workflow and still failed.
output_examples.output: The skill would stop more patching, summarize failed hypotheses, and evaluate whether the architecture is the actual problem.

best_practices: Reproduce the problem and read the full error before proposing any fix.
Test one clear hypothesis at a time with the smallest useful change.
Create a failing test or repeatable check before implementing the final fix.
anti_patterns: Guessing a quick fix before finding the root cause.
Bundling several unrelated changes into one debugging attempt.
Fixing the deepest symptom without tracing where the bad input began.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a bug, test failure, flaky test, build failure, or unexpected behavior needs investigation before code changes.

faq.question: Does it write the fix for me?
faq.answer: It guides the investigation first. After the root cause is clear, it supports a minimal fix and verification plan.

faq.question: Can it help under time pressure?
faq.answer: Yes. The process is designed to reduce wasted fixes when fast guesses feel tempting.

faq.question: Does it require a specific language?
faq.answer: No. The workflow applies broadly, though examples use TypeScript, shell, and common test tooling.

faq.question: Is the included script safe to run?
faq.answer: Run it only in trusted repositories. It executes local npm tests and can trigger package scripts.

faq.question: How does it handle flaky tests?
faq.answer: It encourages waiting for real conditions, adding clear timeouts, and documenting any timing-based waits that remain.
